57: ## Workflow: Constructing an Adaptive Layout
58: 
59: Follow this workflow to implement a layout that adapts to the available `BoxConstraints`.
60: 
61: **Task Progress:**
62: - [ ] Identify the target widget that requires adaptive behavior.
63: - [ ] Wrap the widget tree in a `LayoutBuilder`.
64: - [ ] Extract the `constraints.maxWidth` from the builder callback.
65: - [ ] Define an adaptive breakpoint (e.g., `largeScreenMinWidth = 600`).
66: - [ ] **If `maxWidth > largeScreenMinWidth`:** Return a large-screen layout (e.g., a `Row` placing a navigation sidebar and content area side-by-side).
67: - [ ] **If `maxWidth <= largeScreenMinWidth`:** Return a small-screen layout (e.g., a `Column` or standard navigation-style approach).
68: - [ ] Run validator -> resize the application window -> review layout transitions -> fix overflow errors.
69: 
70: ## Workflow: Optimizing for Large Screens
71: 
72: Follow this workflow to prevent UI elements from stretching unnaturally on large displays.
73: 
74: **Task Progress:**
75: - [ ] Identify full-width components (e.g., `ListView`, text blocks, forms).
76: - [ ] **If optimizing a list:** Convert `ListView.builder` to `GridView.builder` using `SliverGridDelegateWithMaxCrossAxisExtent` to automatically adjust column counts based on window size.
77: - [ ] **If optimizing a form or text block:** Wrap the component in a `ConstrainedBox`.
78: - [ ] Apply `BoxConstraints(maxWidth: [optimal_width])` to the `ConstrainedBox`.
79: - [ ] Wrap the `ConstrainedBox` in a `Center` widget to keep the constrained content centered on large screens.
80: - [ ] Run validator -> test on desktop/tablet target -> review horizontal stretching -> adjust `maxWidth` or grid extents.
81: 
82: ## Examples
83: 
84: ### Adaptive Layout using LayoutBuilder
85: Demonstrates switching between a mobile and desktop layout based on available width.
86: 
87: ```dart
88: import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
89: 
90: const double largeScreenMinWidth = 600.0;
91: 
92: class AdaptiveLayout extends StatelessWidget {
93:   const AdaptiveLayout({super.key});
94: 
95:   @override
96:   Widget build(BuildContext context) {
97:     return LayoutBuilder(
98:       builder: (context, constraints) {
99:         if (constraints.maxWidth > largeScreenMinWidth) {
100:           return _buildLargeScreenLayout();
101:         } else {
102:           return _buildSmallScreenLayout();
103:         }
104:       },
105:     );
106:   }
107: 
108:   Widget _buildLargeScreenLayout() {
109:     return Row(
110:       children: [
111:         const SizedBox(width: 250, child: Placeholder(color: Colors.blue)),
112:         const VerticalDivider(width: 1),
113:         Expanded(child: const Placeholder(color: Colors.green)),
114:       ],
115:     );
116:   }
117: 
118:   Widget _buildSmallScreenLayout() {
119:     return const Placeholder(color: Colors.green);
120:   }
121: }
122: ```

124: ### Constraining Width on Large Screens
125: Demonstrates preventing a widget from consuming all horizontal space.
126: 
127: ```dart
128: import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
129: 
130: class ConstrainedContent extends StatelessWidget {
131:   const ConstrainedContent({super.key});
132: 
133:   @override
134:   Widget build(BuildContext context) {
135:     return Scaffold(
136:       body: Center(
137:         child: ConstrainedBox(
138:           constraints: const BoxConstraints(
139:             maxWidth: 800.0, // Maximum width for readability
140:           ),
141:           child: ListView.builder(
142:             itemCount: 50,
143:             itemBuilder: (context, index) {
144:               return ListTile(
145:                 title: Text('Item $index'),
146:               );
147:             },
148:           ),
149:         ),
150:       ),
151:     );
152:   }
153: }
154: ```
